concerns.text: The power section contains a placeholder ‘[deferred]’ and no concrete sample‑size or detectable‑effect calculation. After BH correction across ~100 taxa, a true ρ≈0.30 may be under‑powered with the assumed ≥30 patients, risking false‑negative conclusions.
Permutation p‑values are generated but the plan does not state that they will be subjected to BH correction. Without multiple‑testing adjustment the empirical p‑values may inflate Type I error.

Reducing each longitudinal trajectory to a single linear slope assumes linear change over time and discards within‑patient variation. This can bias effect estimates and further reduces statistical power, especially when disease progression is non‑linear.

Covariate adjustment is performed by residualizing per‑patient slopes on static covariates (age, sex, levodopa dose). If levodopa dose varies across visits, this approach fails to control for time‑varying confounding; a mixed‑effects model with covariates entered directly would be more appropriate.
